sentences.show: On this day in 1822, a young Frenchman announced he could read a script lost for fourteen centuries.
Napoleon's soldiers had found the key in Egypt: the Rosetta Stone.
One decree, in hieroglyphs, Demotic and Greek.
Many thought hieroglyphs were mystic symbols no one could read.
In London, Thomas Young had worked out only a few signs.
But Jean-François Champollion spoke Coptic, the last form of the Egyptian language.
He ran to find his brother, shouted “I've got it!” — and collapsed.
Thirteen days later, he read his letter to the Academy in Paris.
In the audience sat his rival, Thomas Young.
Soon, they were quarrelling over who deserved the credit.
Every day has a story like this.
